question: A semiconductor material has identical electron and hole concentrations of $6 \times 10^8 \text{ m}^{-3}$ at a specific temperature. It is then doped with an unknown impurity, which causes the electron concentration to spike to $9 \times 10^{12} \text{ m}^{-3}$. Calculate the new hole concentration and identify the resulting extrinsic semiconductor type.
